body.statement:
For every loopless graph \(G\), the zero-allowed model and law sets decompose into their finitely many exact-support strata:
\[
 \mathfrak M^{\le}_{\mathcal I}(G)
 =\bigcup_{F\subseteq G}\mathfrak M_{\mathcal I}(F),
 \qquad
 \mathcal P^{\le}_{\mathcal I}(G)
 =\bigcup_{F\subseteq G}\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(F),                  \tag{19}
\]
where \(F\) ranges over all spanning loopless subgraphs of \(G\).  Each coefficient matrix belongs to the unique stratum with edge set \(\operatorname{supp}(B)\).
body.proof_tex: Take a mechanism in \(\mathfrak M^{\le}_{\mathcal I}(G)\) and let \(F\) be the spanning loopless graph whose edge set is \(\operatorname{supp}(B)\).  By the zero-allowed support condition, \(F\subseteq G\).  The matrix has exact support \(F\), and every other clause---regime solvability, independence, nonconstancy, non-Gaussianity, and surgical intervention---is unchanged.  Hence the mechanism lies in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathcal I}(F)\).  Conversely, exact support \(F\subseteq G\) implies support contained in \(G\), so every exact-stratum mechanism lies in the zero-allowed class.  The stratum is unique because its edge set is the actual support of \(B\).  This proves the first equality in (19).  Applying the response-kernel map to both sides and using the definitions of the two law sets proves the second.  The union is finite because \(G\) has finitely many edges.
